concept.name: High-volume node
concept.definition: A peak in the volume profile — a price zone where traded volume was significantly higher than in neighboring zones. HVNs mark areas of accepted value where buyers and sellers did heavy two-sided business, and price commonly slows or consolidates when it re-enters them.
concept.intuition: An HVN is a crowded marketplace: lots of transactions happened there because both sides found the price acceptable.
concept.mechanics: Read visually from the volume-at-price histogram as local maxima (bulges) spanning several adjacent rows; the profile's point of control lies within the most prominent HVN.
concept.failure_modes: HVN boundaries are fuzzy and row-size dependent; treating a bulge as a precise support/resistance zone fails because the level is a region of past activity, not a price with a queue of orders.
concept.misconceptions: HVNs are not walls — price can slice through an old HVN when the participants who built it are no longer defending their positions; the node records history, not standing interest.
concept.example: The profile shows a bulge at 4,480–4,495; when a selloff reaches the zone, price decelerates into a two-day sideways consolidation inside the node.
